before_question.question: When Machine Wild guarantees a second encounter but the player needs a new hand to take it, what happens to the old hand and to the Machine flare during the replacement?

required_facts: Play Machine Wild faceup outside the hand.
Discard the old hand and draw a new eight-card hand if needed for the guaranteed second encounter.
Return the Machine flare to hand after its effect resolves.

after_question.question: When Machine Wild guarantees a second encounter but the player needs a new hand to take it, what happens to the old hand and to the Machine flare during the replacement? Does its otherwise legal second-encounter guarantee still apply if the completed first encounter was unsuccessful, such as a loss or failed deal?

required_facts: Play Machine Wild faceup outside the hand.
Discard the old hand and draw a new eight-card hand if needed for the guaranteed second encounter.
Return the Machine flare to hand after its effect resolves.

Yes: when otherwise legal Machine Wild applies to this turn, its guarantee permits a second encounter despite a completed first loss or failed deal; the ordinary first-success condition does not defeat that guarantee.
contextual_background: The legal-use/applicability condition is supplied. No full trigger, role, first-placement window, additional encounters beyond the second or remaining flare text is reconstructed.
source_references: 2018 FAQ p16 extraction1543–1550, unqualified second-encounter guarantee and needed new hand; p17 1559–1561, quoted you may always have a second encounter; original rulebook p7/p11 ordinary first-success eligibility.

reason: Previous replacement question supplied the guarantee as a given; it did not ask whether the ordinary first-failure condition defeats it.
primary_support: Unqualified guarantee plus quoted may always; otherwise legal-use condition preserved, no activation window or full card reconstructed.
